title: Two Spoons Later, the Trophy's His
title_candidates: Two Spoons Later, the Trophy's His
From the Spoon Drawer to the Trophy Cabinet
theme: Stuart Neumann completes an eight-year journey from two-time Wooden Spoon holder to first-ever Trophy champion, building his win wire-to-wire rather than inheriting it, while Alex Baker rewrites the course record book at both ends of the scoring table.
opening_hook: Open on Neumann's history — two prior Wooden Spoons and zero Trophy wins across a decade of TEGs — before cutting to the four rounds that ended it; the point isn't suspense (he led throughout) but distance travelled, so the frame is retrospective rather than round-by-round.

trophy_storyline.subject: Stuart Neumann builds and holds the Trophy lead from hole four of R1 to the final putt of R4, winning by 13 after posting the best Stableford score in the field in three of four rounds, on the back of a Trophy record of two prior Wooden Spoons and no wins.
trophy_storyline.why_it_matters: It is Neumann's first-ever Trophy win, and he won it the hard way — by outplaying the field round after round, not by waiting for a rival to fall back.
trophy_storyline.shape: Setup: Neumann draws level for the lead at R1 hole 4 and takes it outright soon after. Turn: his lead only grows — 5, then 7, then 12 points — as he posts the best round in the field in R1, R2 and R3, despite a wild R4 hole-8 quintuple bogey. Resolution: a merely second-best R4 (still ahead of Williams by a point) is more than enough, closing out a 13-point win that Williams could not have overturned even with an ordinary round instead of his worst.
headline_candidates: Two Spoons Later, the Trophy's His
Neumann Finally Gets His Hands On It
Wire to Wire, Spoon to Silverware
trophy_storyline.chosen_headline: Two Spoons Later, the Trophy's His
trophy_storyline.standfirst: Stuart Neumann led the Trophy from the fourth hole of the tournament and was never seriously troubled again, closing out a first career win by 13 points.

jacket_storyline.subject: Gregg Williams wins the Green Jacket by posting the best gross score in the field in all four rounds, stretching his lead from 3 shots to 16 despite repeated mid-round wobbles that never once cost him the outright lead.
jacket_storyline.why_it_matters: It confirms Williams as the week's best pure striker even as the Trophy goes the other way — ordinary handicapping, not a paradox, since Stableford and gross measure different things.
jacket_storyline.shape: Setup: Williams leads the Jacket from R1 by 3. Turn: costly stretches — holes 8-11 in R2, 6-8 in R3, a double bogey at the 9th in R4 — repeatedly knock him about but never threaten his position, because he is also the field's best gross scorer every round. Resolution: David Mullin mounts a spectacular late charge, breaking the Estoril course record with an 80 in R4, but starts the round too far back for it to matter.
headline_candidates: Best in the Field, Every Time
Williams Wears the Jacket Four Rounds Running
Mullin's Record Round Comes a Day Too Late
jacket_storyline.chosen_headline: Best in the Field, Every Time
jacket_storyline.standfirst: Gregg Williams topped the gross leaderboard in every round of the tournament, seeing off a grandstand finish from David Mullin, who broke the Estoril course record along the way.

spoon_storyline.subject: Alex Baker finishes bottom of the Trophy standings in all four rounds and sets new course-worst records at two different venues — Oitavos Dunes in R1 and Estoril in R4 — via a run of blow-up holes that includes a septuple bogey.
spoon_storyline.why_it_matters: The Spoon race was effectively decided by the first hole of R1, but the manner of the defeat — course-worst rounds bracketing the whole tournament — is the funniest and rarest story of the week.
spoon_storyline.shape: Setup: Baker drops to the bottom of the Spoon standings on the very first hole of the tournament and never leaves it. Turn: the position stays static while the holes underneath it get wilder — a sextuple bogey and two quintuple bogeys set a new Oitavos Dunes course-worst in R1, then a septuple bogey and a 14-shot bleed across holes 5-10 set a new Estoril course-worst in R4. Resolution: he finishes 4 points adrift of his own brother, Jon, the closest rival, having been genuinely one of the field's steadier players round-to-round — just steady at the bottom.
headline_candidates: Baker Breaks Two Records — Both the Wrong Way
A Spoon Earned at the First Tee, Confirmed at the Last
spoon_storyline.chosen_headline: Baker Breaks Two Records — Both the Wrong Way
spoon_storyline.standfirst: Alex Baker propped up the Trophy table from the first hole of the tournament and closed it out by setting new course-worst marks at both ends of the week.

discovered_storylines.subject: Both Baker brothers implode at the same hole in the same round — the par-5 12th at Penha Longa in R3 — Jon making a quintuple bogey and Alex a quadruple bogey within overlapping runs of dropped shots.
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: A shared collapse at literally the same hole, between two brothers in the same field, turns a family joke into tournament history.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: both Bakers arrive at Penha Longa's 12th in the middle of otherwise ordinary rounds. Turn: Jon runs up a quintuple bogey and Alex a quadruple bogey at the same hole, each the low point of a three-to-four-hole bleed either side of it. Resolution: neither round recovers — Jon's stretch ends a spell in which he'd twice drawn level for the Jacket lead earlier in the tournament, and Alex's compounds a Spoon campaign already gone.
headline_candidates: The 12th at Penha Longa Claims Both Bakers
Brothers in Arms, Undone at the Same Hole
A Family Disaster, Hole by Hole
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: The 12th at Penha Longa Claims Both Bakers
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Jon and Alex Baker, brothers in the same field, both came unstuck at the same par-5 in Round 3 — one with a quintuple bogey, the other a quadruple.

discovered_storylines.subject: David Mullin follows the worst round of his tournament — a blow-up finish at Penha Longa that leaves him on 30 Stableford points — with an Estoril course-record 80 gross the very next day, the sharpest round-to-round swing in the field.
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: It is the single biggest turnaround of the tournament and produces a genuine all-time course record, even though it arrives too late to trouble the podium.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: Mullin closes R3 at Penha Longa with a quadruple bogey at the 16th, bottoming out at 30 points. Turn: at Estoril in R4 he strings together bogey-free stretches from the 2nd hole onward. Resolution: his 80 gross beats the old Estoril course record by six shots — the standout individual round of the week, delivered a day after his worst.
headline_candidates: A Course Record, One Day After the Wheels Came Off
Mullin's Worst Round Becomes His Best
From 30 to a Record 80: Mullin's Estoril Turnaround
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: A Course Record, One Day After the Wheels Came Off
discovered_storylines.standfirst: David Mullin shot the worst round of his tournament at Penha Longa, then came back the next day to break the Estoril course record.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Alex Baker's run of collapses (seven blow-up beats, course-worst records at two different venues) is real and drives the Spoon story, but the report's primary frame stays Neumann's origin story — his first Trophy win after two prior Spoons.

why_the_champion_won: Neumann won by building, not inheriting: the best round in the field in three of four rounds, never worse than second, and a lead that only grew — Williams was already beaten before his own worst round even factored in.
